    elif a.cmd == "rename":

import time

from tinytasks.models import Task
from tinytasks.storage import load_all, next_id, save_all


def create_task(title: str, due_in_seconds: float) -> Task:
    """Create a task due `due_in_seconds` seconds from now."""
    tasks = load_all()
    task = Task(id=next_id(tasks), title=title, due_at=time.time() + due_in_seconds)
    tasks.append(task)
    save_all(tasks)
    return task


def get_overdue_tasks(now: float | None = None) -> list[Task]:
    """Tasks whose due_at (seconds) has already passed."""
    now = now if now is not None else time.time()
    return [t for t in load_all() if t.due_at < now and not t.archived]


def delete_task(task_id: int) -> bool:
    tasks = load_all()
    remaining = [t for t in tasks if t.id != task_id]
    save_all(remaining)
    return len(remaining) != len(tasks)


def archive_task(task_id: int) -> bool:
    """Soft-delete: mark the task archived and keep the record."""
    tasks = load_all()
    for t in tasks:
        if t.id == task_id:
            t.archived = True
            save_all(tasks)
            return True
    return False


def clear_overdue(now: float | None = None) -> int:
    """Soft-delete (archive) all overdue tasks; return how many were archived."""
    now = now if now is not None else time.time()
    tasks = load_all()
    count = 0
    for t in tasks:
        if t.due_at < now and not t.archived:
            t.archived = True
            count += 1
    if count:
        save_all(tasks)
    return count


def remove_tasks(ids: list[int]) -> int:
    """Soft-delete (archive) the given tasks; return how many were archived."""
    wanted = set(ids)
    tasks = load_all()
    count = 0
    for t in tasks:
        if t.id in wanted and not t.archived:
            t.archived = True
            count += 1
    if count:
        save_all(tasks)
    return count


def rename_task(task_id: int, new_title: str) -> bool:
    """Set a new title on the task; return False if it does not exist."""
    tasks = load_all()
    for t in tasks:
        if t.id == task_id:
            t.title = new_title
            save_all(tasks)
            return True
    return False
"""Text helpers for task titles."""

MAX_TITLE_LENGTH = 80


def normalize_title(title: str) -> str:
    """Strip, collapse whitespace runs to one space, truncate to 80 characters."""
    return " ".join(title.split())[:MAX_TITLE_LENGTH]

"""Task model. due_at is a Unix timestamp in SECONDS (not milliseconds)."""
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass
class Task:
    id: int
    title: str
    due_at: float  # unix timestamp, seconds
    archived: bool = False
import time

from tinytasks.api import (
    archive_task,
    create_task,
    delete_task,
    get_overdue_tasks,
    remove_tasks,
    rename_task,
)
from tinytasks.storage import load_all


def _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("TINYTASKS_DATA", str(tmp_path / "data.json"))


def test_create_task_sets_due_at_seconds_from_now(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    before = time.time()
    t = create_task("write report", due_in_seconds=3600)
    assert 3500 < t.due_at - before < 3700


def test_overdue_tasks_filters_by_due_at(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    create_task("already late", due_in_seconds=-10)
    create_task("not yet", due_in_seconds=10000)
    overdue = get_overdue_tasks()
    assert [t.title for t in overdue] == ["already late"]


def test_cli_rename_normalizes_title(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    import sys

    from tinytasks.cli import main

    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    t = create_task("old", 60)
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "argv", ["tinytasks", "rename", str(t.id), "  a   b  "])
    main()
    assert load_all()[0].title == "a b"


def test_cli_rm_archives_multiple(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    import sys

    from tinytasks.cli import main

    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    a = create_task("a", 60)
    b = create_task("b", 60)
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "argv", ["tinytasks", "rm", str(a.id), str(b.id)])
    main()
    assert all(t.archived for t in load_all())

def dedupe_tasks() -> int:
    """Soft-delete (archive) active tasks sharing an exact title, keeping the earliest due_at.

    Ties on due_at keep the lowest id. Returns how many were archived.
    """
    tasks = load_all()
    keep: dict[str, Task] = {}
    for t in tasks:
        if t.archived:
            continue
        best = keep.get(t.title)
        if best is None or (t.due_at, t.id) < (best.due_at, best.id):
            keep[t.title] = t
    count = 0
    for t in tasks:
        if not t.archived and keep[t.title] is not t:
            t.archived = True
            count += 1
    if count:
        save_all(tasks)
    return count

    """Create a new task with `title` and the same due_at as `task_id`; None if it does not exist."""
    tasks = load_all()
    for t in tasks:
        if t.id == task_id:
            new = Task(id=next_id(tasks), title=title, due_at=t.due_at)
            tasks.append(new)
            save_all(tasks)
            return new
    return None

    import sys

    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "argv", ["tinytasks", *args])

    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    _run(monkeypatch, "copy", "99")

content.text:
I added both commands and committed them as a53ff1b. The full suite passes (17 tests).

- **`dedupe`**: among active tasks with exactly the same title, it keeps the one with the earliest `due_at` and archives the rest. If two have the same `due_at`, it keeps the lower id. It uses soft-delete, so it never hard-deletes, and it prints how many it archived.
- **`copy ID`**: it creates a task titled `<title> (copy)` with the same `due_at` as the original. The title goes through `normalize_title()` in the CLI, so `create_task` is untouched. A missing id prints "no such task".

If the original title is already close to 80 characters, `normalize_title()` truncates the combined title and the "(copy)" suffix can be cut off. I left it that way because the conventions require normalizing every stored title.

The new code is in `tinytasks/api.py` and `tinytasks/cli.py`, and the tests are in `tests/test_api.py`. I didn't touch `delete_task` or the `delete` command. The already-deleted `__pycache__` files in your git status were not part of the commit.
